description: An Inventor proposes warehouse pick-order heuristics while an independent Referee accepts a new champion only after the same fixed benchmarks show fewer training steps and no withheld regression. Public grid replays make the robot’s detours and return to the depot visible.

facts: A robot must visit every pick location and return to the depot; obstacles are impassable.
All path legs use exact shortest paths on the same four-neighbor grid.
Candidate heuristics choose the visit order; lower total walking distance is better.
Four fixed training fixtures and three fixed withheld fixtures evaluate every challenger.
Promotion requires fewer training steps and no regression on the withheld fixtures.
Replays show actual training paths. Held-out locations remain private.

last_decision.reason: Inventor: test a nearby vertical weight against the current champion. Benchmark runner: the champion measures 186 training and 148 withheld steps; this candidate’s full results are not yet known. Independent referee: only computed results can show whether it improves training without withheld regression. Alternatives: rest and retain the champion without a new comparison; replay training-1, which reveals one route but does not evaluate all fixtures.
